label: accelerationTime
comment:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.

Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds

* Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]], or use [[valueReference]] with a [[QuantitativeValue]] of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.
enriched_comment: Relates a vehicle to the quantitative duration required to accelerate from a starting speed to a target speed. Also called "zero to sixty time", "acceleration duration", "time to speed". Examples: [Sports Car - accelerationTime - "3.2 seconds"], [Electric Sedan - accelerationTime - "4.5 seconds"], [Motorcycle - accelerationTime - "2.8 seconds"].
embedding_text: accelerationTime (from Vehicle to QuantitativeValue): Relates a vehicle to the quantitative duration required to accelerate from a starting speed to a target speed. Also called "zero to sixty time", "acceleration duration", "time to speed".

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org style guide .
enriched_comment: Relates any entity to an additional, more specific RDF class or type URI. Also called "rdf:type", "extra type", "semantic class". Examples: [Local Business - additionalType - "https://schema.org/Restaurant"], [Book - additionalType - "http://vocab.org/BookType"], [Product - additionalType - "https://example.com/CustomProductClass"].
embedding_text: additionalType (from Thing to Text or URL): Relates any entity to an additional, more specific RDF class or type URI. Also called "rdf:type", "extra type", "semantic class".

Also called "exercise variable", "workout progression", "additional prescription detail". Examples: [Rehab Plan - additionalVariable - "Perform exercises in order listed."], [Weight Training - additionalVariable - "Increase weight by 5 lbs every week."], [Cardio Plan - additionalVariable - "Maintain heart rate between 120-140 bpm."].
embedding_text: additionalVariable (from ExercisePlan to Text): Relates an exercise plan to any additional instructions or variables, such as exercise order or progression details, prescribed to the patient. Also called "exercise variable", "workout progression", "additional prescription detail".

label: fuelConsumption
comment:
The amount of fuel consumed for traveling a particular distance or temporal duration with the given vehicle (e.g. liters per 100 km).

* Note 1: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for liters per 100 km. Use [[unitText]] to indicate the unit of measurement, e.g. L/100 km.
* Note 2: There are two ways of indicating the fuel consumption, [[fuelConsumption]] (e.g. 8 liters per 100 km) and [[fuelEfficiency]] (e.g. 30 miles per gallon). They are reciprocal.
* Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use [[valueReference]] to link the value for the fuel consumption to another value.

Distinct from fuelEfficiency, which is the reciprocal measure (distance per unit fuel).

label: fuelEfficiency

* Note 1: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for miles per gallon or kilometers per liter. Use [[unitText]] to indicate the unit of measurement, e.g. mpg or km/L.
* Note 2: There are two ways of indicating the fuel consumption, [[fuelConsumption]] (e.g. 8 liters per 100 km) and [[fuelEfficiency]] (e.g. 30 miles per gallon). They are reciprocal.
* Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use [[valueReference]] to link the value for the fuel economy to another value.

label: geoContains
comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a containing geometry to a contained geometry. enriched_comment: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoContains another GeospatialGeometry or Place if the subject completely encloses the object, with at least one interior point of the object also in the interior of the subject. Also called "encloses", "encompasses", "has within". Examples: "The country geoContains 'a specific city'.", "The park geoContains 'a playground'.", "The polygon geoContains 'a smaller polygon'." Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relationship (object is within subject).

Also called "encloses", "encompasses", "has within". Examples: "The country geoContains 'a specific city'.", "The park geoContains 'a playground'.", "The polygon geoContains 'a smaller polygon'."

label: geoCoveredBy

Also called "is covered by", "lies within", "is encompassed by". Examples: "The city is geoCoveredBy 'the state'.", "The small island is geoCoveredBy 'the ocean'.", "The point is geoCoveredBy 'the polygon'." comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a covering geometry to a covered geometry. "Every point of b is a point of (the interior or boundary of) a". As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).

label: geoCrosses
comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a geometry to another that crosses it: "a crosses b: they have some but not all interior points in common, and the dimension of the intersection is less than that of at least one of them". Also called "intersects and passes through", "crosses over", "traverses". Examples: "A road geoCrosses 'a river'.", "The flight path geoCrosses 'several states'.", "A line segment geoCrosses 'a polygon'." Distinct from geoIntersects, which is a more general intersection.

label: geoDisjoint
comment: Represents spatial relations in which two geometries (or the places they represent) are topologically disjoint: "they have no point in common. They form a set of disconnected geometries." (A symmetric relationship, as defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).)
enriched_comment: A GeospatialGeometry or Place is geoDisjoint from another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they have no points in common and are topologically disconnected. Also called "separate from", "not overlapping", "disconnected from". Examples: "Two islands are geoDisjoint.", "The two buildings are geoDisjoint.", "The point is geoDisjoint from 'the polygon'." Distinct from geoIntersects, which implies common points.

Also called "separate from", "not overlapping", "disconnected from". Examples: "Two islands are geoDisjoint.", "The two buildings are geoDisjoint.", "The point is geoDisjoint from 'the polygon'."

label: geoEquals
comment: Represents spatial relations in which two geometries (or the places they represent) are topologically equal, as defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM). "Two geometries are topologically equal if their interiors intersect and no part of the interior or boundary of one geometry intersects the exterior of the other" (a symmetric relationship).
enriched_comment: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoEquals another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they are topologically identical, meaning their interiors intersect and neither's interior or boundary intersects the other's exterior. Also called "is geographically equal to", "same location as", "identical geometry". Examples: "Two representations of the same park geoEquals each other.", "The administrative boundary geoEquals 'the natural boundary'.", "The two polygons geoEquals if they define the exact same area."
embedding_text: geoEquals (from GeospatialGeometry or Place to GeospatialGeometry or Place): A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoEquals another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they are topologically identical, meaning their interiors intersect and neither's interior or boundary intersects the other's exterior. label: geoIntersects
comment: Represents spatial relations in which two geometries (or the places they represent) have at least one point in common. As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).
enriched_comment: A GeospatialGeometry or Place geoIntersects another GeospatialGeometry or Place if they share at least one common point. Also called "overlaps with", "touches", "crosses". Examples: "The road geoIntersects 'the forest'.", "The two cities' boundaries geoIntersects.", "The point geoIntersects 'the line'." Distinct from geoDisjoint, which means no common points.

label: geoOverlaps

label: gtin
comment: A Global Trade Item Number ([GTIN](https://www.gs1.org/standards/id-keys/gtin)). GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. A correct [[gtin]] value should be a valid GTIN, which means that it should be an all-numeric string of either 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, or a "GS1 Digital Link" URL based on such a string. The numeric component should also have a [valid GS1 check digit](https://www.gs1.org/services/check-digit-calculator) and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also [GS1's GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Trade_Item_Number) for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged. The [[gtin]] property generalizes the earlier [[gtin8]], [[gtin12]], [[gtin13]], and [[gtin14]] properties. The GS1 [digital link specifications](https://www.gs1.org/standards/Digital-Link/) expresses GTINs as URLs (URIs, IRIs, etc.). Digital Links should be populated into the [[hasGS1DigitalLink]] attribute. Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details.
enriched_comment: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin, which is its Global Trade Item Number, a numeric identifier for trade items. Also called "Global Trade Item Number", "product identifier", "barcode number". Examples: "The Product has a gtin of '0123456789012'.", "This Offer's gtin is 'https://example.com/gtin/1234567890123'.", "The gtin identifies the specific product variant." Distinct from sku, which is a stock-keeping unit for internal use.

Examples: "The Product has a gtin of '0123456789012'.", "This Offer's gtin is 'https://example.com/gtin/1234567890123'.", "The gtin identifies the specific product variant."

label: gtin12
comment: The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. The GTIN-12 is the 12-digit GS1 Identification Key composed of a U.P.C. Company Prefix, Item Reference, and Check Digit used to identify trade items. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.
enriched_comment: A Demand, Offer, or Product has a gtin12, which is its 12-digit Global Trade Item Number (UPC). Also called "UPC code", "GTIN-12", "product barcode". Distinct from gtin, which is a general GTIN, and gtin13, gtin14, gtin8 for other specific GTIN lengths.

label: handlingTime
comment: The typical delay between the receipt of the order and the goods either leaving the warehouse or being prepared for pickup, in case the delivery method is on site pickup. In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY). This is by common convention assumed to mean business days (if a unitCode is used, coded as "d"), i.e. only counting days when the business normally operates. In the context of [[ShippingService]], use the [[ServicePeriod]] format, that contains the same information in a structured form, with cut-off time, business days and duration.
enriched_comment: handlingTime describes the typical duration a ShippingDeliveryTime or ShippingService takes to process an order before the goods are dispatched or ready for pickup. Also called "processing time", "preparation time", "dispatch time", "order fulfillment time". Examples: A ShippingDeliveryTime has a handlingTime of "2 business days". A ShippingService has a handlingTime of "1-3 days". A ShippingDeliveryTime has a handlingTime of a ServicePeriod specifying a cut-off time and duration.

comment: Describes the amount that can be redeemed from this incentive. [[QuantitativeValue]]: Use this for incentives based on price (either raw amount or percentage-based). For a raw amount example, "You can claim $2,500 - $7,500 from the total cost of installation" would be represented as the following: { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", “minValue”: 2500, “maxValue”: 7500, "unitCode": "USD" } [[QuantitativeValue]] can also be used for percentage amounts. label: iso6523Code
comment: An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous.
enriched_comment: An Organization has an ISO 6523 code, which is Text, representing its international organization identifier. Also called "ISO organization ID", "international entity code", "standard organization identifier". Examples: "The Organization has an iso6523Code '0060:123456789' (DUNS).", "The company's iso6523Code is used for international transactions.", "The Organization's iso6523Code identifies it globally."

label: lowPrice
comment:
The lowest price of all offers available.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
enriched_comment: This property specifies the lowest price among all available offers within a subject AggregateOffer. Also called "minimum price", "cheapest price", "starting price". Examples: "Product X AggregateOffer lowPrice 9.99", "Service Y AggregateOffer lowPrice 50.00", "Event Ticket AggregateOffer lowPrice 25.50". Distinct from highPrice, which specifies the highest price among available offers.

label: maintainer
comment: A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. A maintainer is a [[Person]] or [[Organization]] that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.
enriched_comment: This property identifies the person or organization responsible for managing contributions to and/or publication of a subject creative work, such as a dataset or software package. Also called "managed by", "curated by", "supported by". Examples: "Software Package A maintainer 'Open Source Community'", "Dataset B maintainer 'University Research Group'", "Project C maintainer 'John Doe'".
embedding_text: maintainer (from CreativeWork to Organization or Person): This property identifies the person or organization responsible for managing contributions to and/or publication of a subject creative work, such as a dataset or software package. Also called "managed by", "curated by", "supported by".

To discourage over-use, and reflecting intial usecases, the property is expected only on [[Product]] and [[Offer]], rather than [[Thing]]. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. The property is intended for the case when items (primarily [[Product]] and [[Offer]]) have extra URLs hosted on an additional "mobile site" alongside the main one. Distinct from url, which is the general URL for the page, ideally responsive.

label: openingHours
comment:
The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.

* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.
* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. 
* Here is an example: <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Tu,Th 16:00-20:00">Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm</time> .
* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Mo-Su">Monday through Sunday, all day</time> .
enriched_comment: A CivicStructure or LocalBusiness has opening hours, which are its general operating times specified as a weekly time range. Also called business hours, hours of operation, open times. Examples: A restaurant has opening hours 'Mo-Fr 09:00-17:00'. A museum has opening hours 'Tu-Su 10:00-18:00'. A store has opening hours 'Mo-Su 08:00-22:00'. Distinct from openingHoursSpecification, which provides structured details about opening hours.

label: price
comment:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:

* Use the [[priceCurrency]] property (with standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS) and other currency types, e.g. "Ithaca HOUR") instead of including [ambiguous symbols](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_sign#Currencies_that_use_the_dollar_or_peso_sign) such as '$' in the value.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
* Note that both [RDFa](http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml-rdfa-primer/#using-the-content-attribute) and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
enriched_comment: price is the Number or Text representing the monetary cost of an Offer, PriceSpecification, DonateAction, or TradeAction. Also called cost, value, rate, charge. Examples: A product offer price 19.99. A service price "Free". A price specification price 100.

label: speakable
comment: Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.
enriched_comment: Relates a web page or article to a specification or URL indicating which sections are optimized for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech target", "audio-friendly section", "speakable content". Examples: [News Article - speakable - "article-summary-id"], [Recipe Page - speakable - "ingredients-list-selector"], [FAQ Page - speakable - "top-answers-xpath"].
embedding_text: speakable (from Article or WebPage to SpeakableSpecification or URL): Relates a web page or article to a specification or URL indicating which sections are optimized for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech target", "audio-friendly section", "speakable content".

The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.

Distinct from license, which directly specifies the active license.
embedding_text: usageInfo (from CreativeWork to CreativeWork or URL): Relates a creative work to a document or URL containing detailed information about its licensing, citation guidelines, or commercial usage rights. Also called 'licensing options', 'usage guidelines', 'rights information'.

label: value
comment:
The value of a [[QuantitativeValue]] (including [[Observation]]) or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
